test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What was the major purpose of the ‘permit license raj’ from the 1960s to 1980s in India?

options.text: Government allowing nationalised banks to lend to private companies
Government allowing public sector undertakings to produce goods
Government allowing only foreign companies to sell goods in India
Government allowing private companies to produce goods

solution:
The correct answer is __**Government allowing private companies to produce goods. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Permit License Raj:-**

 
 
• **The Permit License Raj was a system of extensive government regulation and control over the Indian economy from the 1950s to the early 1990s. **
 
• It was characterized by a web of regulations, permits, and licenses that businesses had to obtain in order to operate.
 
• The system was intended to protect Indian industry, promote self-reliance, and ensure regional equality.
 
• However, it also led to widespread corruption, inefficiency, and a stifling of economic growth. 
 
• **The major purpose of the ‘permit license raj’ from the 1960s to 1980s in India was that the Government allowing private companies to produce goods.** 
 
• **Key features of the Permit License Raj:**
 
 
• Businesses had to obtain licenses from the government for everything from starting a new company to expanding an existing one.
 
• The government also controlled the prices of many goods and services.
 
• Imports were heavily restricted, and businesses were often required to use Indian-made products, even if they were of inferior quality.
 
• The Permit License Raj was a major obstacle to economic development in India. It led to widespread corruption, inefficiency, and a stifling of innovation.
